slides.texte_overlay:
unusual hobbies that
make you better smarter
Learning to identify trees and birds. Walking becomes a treasure hunt. Naming what you see trains memory and attention in a calm, surprising way.
Restoring old furniture. Sanding, repairing, painting. You learn patience, problem-solving and how things were built, and you end up with something unique.
Learning basic astronomy. A star map, a clear night, a pair of binoculars. Finding planets and constellations makes you feel curious and small in the best way.
Writing short stories. Ten minutes a day, any idea. Writing fiction trains imagination, structure and empathy all at once. Nobody has to read them.
Feeding your curiosity every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives every hobby I try a deeper meaning.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives every hobby I try a deeper meaning.

slides.texte_overlay: Learning to play poker properly. Not for money, for thinking. Probability, patience and reading people are skills that help in every part of life.
Building a small garden on your balcony. Herbs, tomatoes, peppers. Planning, waiting and learning from mistakes makes you calmer and smarter.
